scope.method: Deduplicate reactAlignmentPartWitnessesFor(family, axis) by witness id across every REACT_ALIGNMENT_FAMILIES entry, then inspect the reference CSS and TSX owner. Source expressions are recorded verbatim; this artifact contains no browser measurements.

dispositions.token-owner: The selected rendered part owns an intrinsic inset, gap, compensation, canvas, or border-aware row/box relationship.
dispositions.supporting-evidence: The witness observes a dependent/keyline/state of another recorded owner and does not create a second spacing owner.
dispositions.non-spacing-boundary: The witness is paint, an atomic leaf with no spacing relationship, or layout composition outside the component-spacing taxonomy.

scope.measurementCaveat: Exact ownerSelector identifies the element that owns each CSS relationship; it does not license arithmetic from a witness outer box to a descendant text keyline. In the adorned Text specimen, Astra measured Site outer-to-text as 38.406px: wrapper border plus child input padding cannot be summed to claim an 8px outside keyline because prefix/suffix slots intervene.

records.reason: Primary owner for the shared single-line framed-field contract. The wrapper owns the border and compensation; the text-bearing input owns the inline and block padding.
records.measurementCaveat: This catalog specimen is adorned with both prefix and suffix. The child input owns its padding, but the wrapper-to-text distance also crosses the prefix slot. Astra measured Site outer-to-text as 38.406px; do not derive or report an 8px outside keyline by adding wrapper border and input padding.

records.reason: The Number wrapper and input leaf repeat the shared TextInput frame/padding contract. The catalog specimen is adorned, so prefix/suffix geometry is dispositioned separately by the trailing-artwork witness.
records.measurementCaveat: The Number specimen renders prefix and suffix flex items. The child input's padding is source-owned by the input, but an outer-wrapper-to-text measurement crosses adornment geometry and cannot be treated as border plus input padding.

relationships.contract: field adornment gap plus field edge inset
relationships.sourceExpression: var(--form-field-inline-gap, var(--form-field-inline-gap-default)); prefix start and suffix end use var(--ds-form-field-padding-inline-start/end)

records.reason: The adornment slots, not the shared frame, own the intrinsic text-to-artwork gap and restore the field inset at the outside edge. The witness name says trailing artwork, but the same CSS also covers a leading prefix.
The label is the dependent keyline of the option row; it does not own a second inset or nudge.
The real button receives ds-field-frame and owns its border-aware edge insets, child gap, and trailing row compensation.

relationships.sourceExpression: owned by parent gap: var(--form-field-inline-gap, var(--form-field-inline-gap-default))

records.reason: The preview is a fixed painted leaf. Its position supports the trigger's gap/inset contract; its own width, height, and border are paint canvas geometry, not another spacing owner.

relationships.contract: color-trigger field inset after child gap
relationships.sourceExpression: parent padding via --ds-box-padding-inline-* and gap via --form-field-inline-gap

records.reason: The value span has no padding or margin; it observes the trigger owner's keyline.
This nested input deliberately overrides both framed-box inset axes and owns its own real border-aware padding. It is not equivalent to the regular single-line field row.
The native date control is a direct-chrome consumer of the same field and row owner as TextInput.
The native datetime-local control is a direct-chrome consumer of the shared field owner.

relationships.contract: field inset with trailing artwork canvas

records.reason: Single-select is a distinct field variant because it reserves the shared trailing-artwork canvas. The multiple-select no-artwork variant is recorded as an extra.
Textarea owns a multiline content surface and a public block-padding hook, so its vertical behavior cannot be cited as equivalent to the single-line row without measurement.
The native time control is a direct-chrome consumer of the shared field owner.

relationships.contract: shared field start inset and input-to-reveal gap

records.reason: The frame and text start reuse the shared field owner; the distinct trailing reveal spacing is owned by the reveal action record.
records.measurementCaveat: Wrapper border/compensation, child-input padding, and reveal-button padding have different owner selectors. End-side outer-to-text geometry must include the intervening reveal action rather than collapsing these relationships into one field inset.

records.reason: The country leaf owns the outer field inset on one side and the intrinsic gap to the internal divider on the other.
The telephone leaf owns the divider gap and the opposite outside field inset.
Catalog oracle zero-layout-paint is contradicted by source: this is a real border on the country select and participates in its box geometry. It must be accounted with the two adjacent internal gaps.
The selected node is the fixed-width Range wrapper; its child NumberInput supplies the field geometry. The parent-to-slider gap is a missing owner recorded in extras.
The track is pseudo-element paint centered inside the range element's thumb-sized box. It does not define component inset or inter-child spacing.
Thumb size and centering are native-control paint facts, not padding, gap, margin, or container inset.
A star is an atomic interactive paint canvas. The rating cluster, not each star, owns the spacing between stars; that missing owner is recorded in extras.
The text is a dependent child of the visible label/card surface and adds no padding or margin.
The filename clears inherited paragraph margins/padding and is positioned entirely by the file row owner.
The size span is margin- and padding-free; the file row owns its separation and outside inset.
The combobox input frame is another composite consumer of the shared single-line field contract; its reset action is a separate intrinsic owner.
records.measurementCaveat: The wrapper owns border and compensation, the input child owns row/inline padding, and the reset button owns its action inset. A wrapper-to-text measurement cannot assign all three to the frame.

records.reason: MultipleCombobox mounts the same input frame as SingleCombobox. Its selected-chip strip is a separate owner recorded by chip and extra records.
records.measurementCaveat: The input-frame wrapper and its input child retain split border/compensation versus padding ownership. Selected chips live outside that frame and must not be included in its field-inset arithmetic.

records.reason: This locally styled chip owns bespoke compact padding and an internal remove gap; it does not consume the shared Chip or nested-row contract.
The form intrinsically owns vertical separation between fields. Its subgrid columns are external layout and are recorded as a boundary extra.
The reusable Field wrapper owns the label-to-payload relationship. Its leading-description variant and payload internal stack are separate relationships recorded in extras.
The reveal button is a nested action inside the already seated field row; it owns only the input-to-icon gap and trailing field edge inset, not another vertical row.
The real dashed button is a ds-field-frame owner. Its family label as a direct action does not change its actual field-framed geometry.
The nested remove button owns a local inline hit-area inset while deliberately adding no block row geometry.
The reset action consumes the action inset horizontally but explicitly suppresses Button's independent row ledger because the combobox field owns the line.
Primary owner for the shared ToggleWrapper control row. It owns the marker gap, row seating, compensation, and first-line marker offset.
The row contract is identical to the checkbox wrapper. The switch's wider track/knob canvas is a distinct geometry variant recorded in extras.

The option row owns its marker relationship. The group inset variable is referenced but is not declared anywhere in the reference worktree, so no resolved inset value or valid group assignment can be claimed from source alone.
The glyph fills the star canvas and adds no inset, gap, or margin. The cluster gap is the spacing owner.
Adding an image changes the row's intrinsic content floor through the shared ledger; this is a real geometry-changing variant, not merely marker paint.
The remove icon is a dependent inside the same selected-chip owner; it has no independent margin or padding.
The atomic radio consumes the shared marker canvas but intentionally owns no label gap; a named host row must supply that relationship.
The file item is the actual bordered row owner; filename, size, remove action, and optional thumbnail are dependents or variants within it.
Options own edge-to-edge fill-safe content padding; trailing compensation is folded into block-end padding by the in-box row contract.
Despite the catalog's border-aware-inset oracle, the grid has no border or padding. It owns only inter-swatch gaps; the popover owns the outside inset.
Selected/focused state changes border color and adds a shadow without changing border width, padding, or occupied layout.
The visible label/card is the real border-aware surface owner. It uses the default surface framed-box contract, unlike form floating panels marked ds-field-frame.
Selection and focus repaint an already reserved border and add shadow only; the frame geometry remains owned by alignment-rich-choices-frame.

The popover is a real box owner, but TSX marks it ds-field-frame, so its actual insets derive from the field outer inset and row nudge rather than the default surface inset. This is taxonomy pressure against assuming its catalog family.

relationships.sourceExpression: var(--ds-box-padding-block-start) var(--ds-box-padding-block-end), with --ds-box-border-block-start: var(--form-input-border-width) and --ds-box-inset-block: var(--form-group-gap, var(--form-group-gap-default))

records.reason: The popover hex row owns an asymmetric real top separator and border-aware block inset; it has zero inline surface inset and a local child gap.

relationships.sourceExpression: ds-field-frame border inputs; padding reset to 0

records.reason: The list owns a real border and anchor offset but deliberately resets framed-box padding so option fills reach the edge. Its content inset belongs to each option row, not the list.
FileUpload uses the same reusable Field wrapper as TextField; this selector adds no file-specific spacing rule.
The input shell intrinsically separates the picker and the file-list region. The file-list's own inter-row gap is a distinct missing owner recorded in extras.
Primary owner for shared unboxed field copy. It owns typography-alignment padding/margin and defaults to the field edge horizontally.
Description has the same geometry declaration as Label; only color differs.
Error copy has the same geometry declaration as Label; validation changes color only.

relationships.contract: typographic required-marker separation; normalization decision pending

extras.reason: The required asterisk is a real pseudo-element with a typographic gap, independently owned from the label and control-row marker lane. Capture its pseudo style; the ch-based fallback is not evidence for a new spacing bucket.

relationships.contract: field adornment gap and outside inset

extras.reason: The Text specimen renders both prefix and suffix slots, but the catalog has no witness on them (its trailing-artwork witness is attached to Number). These slots change the content keyline and reserve intrinsic adornment space.

relationships.contract: plain field inset without trailing artwork
relationships.sourceExpression: var(--ds-form-field-padding-inline-end); :not([multiple]) artwork override does not apply

extras.reason: Multiple select deliberately restores platform listbox appearance and does not reserve the single-select chevron canvas; it is a geometry-changing variant absent from the catalog.
The native select witness sees reserved end padding, but no catalog witness directly accounts for the absolutely positioned artwork canvas and its logical-edge anchoring.
Catalog witnesses cover both children independently but omit the parent-owned gap between them.
The catalog selects stars/glyphs, but the cluster is the only spacing owner between stars.
Option witnesses capture within-row marker geometry but omit the parent-owned spacing between wrapped, stacked, or columnar options.
The frame witness covers each card, not the grid-owned gap between cards.
The field witness names the outer label-to-payload gap, but the payload grid independently owns description/control/error separation.
This structural state replaces the default label-to-payload gap and is a geometry-changing Field variant not separately witnessed.
Catalog toggle witnesses select only the control row; the outer ToggleWrapper owns spacing among optional heading, control row, description, and error.
Hex-only ColorInput moves the frame from the nested input to the row and makes the input borderless, a different owner graph from the popover specimen.
The input shell gap separates major regions; the list independently owns separation between repeated file rows.
Chip witnesses capture one chip's internal geometry but omit the wrapping container's gap and its margin before the input.

relationships.sourceExpression: --switch-knob-inset: 1px; translate derives from track width, knob size, and both insets

extras.reason: The shared toggle-row witness does not account for the switch's 2:1 marker canvas or knob inset/travel, which differ from checkbox geometry.
The form inherits its columns from the containing application grid. This is layout composition, not a component inset bucket; only the form's row-gap is intrinsic.
These hooks place Field regions into the parent subgrid and may be set by application composition. They do not establish intrinsic edge padding or a component spacing token.

taxonomyPressure: The source reference ds-global-form Choices stylesheet consumes --ds-leading-mark-group-inset-bare, but that custom property is not declared anywhere in the reference worktree. The bare group inset is therefore unresolved and cannot support a measured/token assignment from source alone.

alignment-phone-input-country-divider is cataloged as zero-layout-paint, but source implements border-inline-end on the country select. It is a layout-bearing internal divider and must be accounted with the adjacent gaps.
alignment-color-input-swatch-grid is cataloged with a border-aware-inset oracle, but the grid owns no border or padding; it owns only row/column gaps. The parent popover owns its outside inset.

ColorInput popover and FileUpload drop zone are framed panels/buttons marked ds-field-frame. They consume field outside-edge/row-nudge geometry, not the default surface framed-box insets suggested by their catalog families.

Combobox list is also marked ds-field-frame but resets padding to zero; its options own action-inline and in-box block padding. Treating the list itself as a padded sectioned panel would double-count the inset.

The FORM catalog undercounts container-owned relationships: parent gaps for Range, Rating, Choices, RichChoices, Field payloads, ToggleWrapper, file lists, and selected Combobox chips are absent even though they change rendered geometry.

The multiple-select, inline ColorInput, thumbnail-bearing file row, switch track, and text/number adornment forms are geometry-changing variants. A component-name-level denominator would collapse materially different owner graphs.

Shared field geometry is genuinely centralized: Text, plain Number, Date, DateTime, Time, and Combobox input frames are dependents of one border-aware field/regular-row owner. Select artwork, Textarea multiline block behavior, Password reveal, Phone partitions, and nested Color hex input are not equivalent extensions of that owner.

Unboxed Label, Description, and Error copy share one typography-alignment owner; Description and Error are evidence dependents, while Field/Toggle/Form wrappers independently own semantic gaps around those leaves.
Form and Field subgrid column placement is an explicit application-layout boundary. It must remain outside component spacing buckets even though the same elements intrinsically own vertical gaps.

Composite witness geometry must retain split ownership. In Text, Number, Password, and Combobox, the outer wrapper owns real borders and trailing compensation while the child input owns padding; adornment slots/actions own intervening gaps. A measured outer-to-text distance is not the algebraic sum of wrapper border and child padding when another flex item intervenes.
